graphEvents.label: What sets the cli lane time inside upgrade-legacy
74 CLI spawns each cost a bash plus two node processes
Vitest reports import as a sum over files, not wall time

label: The cli suite is one 2370-line file with 65 tests over a single shared sandbox copied in beforeAll: 3115 files and 35.8 MB excluding node_modules, then git init and a full-tree baseline commit.

The file's dominant work is process creation: 74 runUpgrade call sites each spawn node upgrade-legacy.mjs, and every packet validation spawns bash validate.sh, which spawns two more node processes (dist-freshness check and validation orchestrator), so one assertion can cost three or four process starts.

The double validation is by design, not waste: validateAll validates the whole scope before any repair and a repaired packet is validated again to prove the repair; neither pass can be removed without dropping a guarantee.

Bare process startup is not the cost: node -e '' measures 0.020 s and bash and git start in under 0.005 s, so 74 node starts total about 1.5 s; the seconds are inside each child's module load and work.

The freshness check validate.sh runs before every validation is cheap: the watched source set for the validation-orchestrator entry is 16 files and 344 KB, so it costs startup plus a small hash rather than a tree walk.
Three of five describe blocks reset the sandbox after every test and two do not, so 58 of 65 tests are provably order-independent and shardable while 7 are not proven independent.

Each reset is paid once per test and includes git reset --hard, removal of six paths, and refreshCopiedDistMtimes walking the copied runtime tree to utimes every file under a dist path, 734 such files in the real tree.

Vitest reports import time as collectTime = sum(files, file => file.collectDuration) printed beside the wall executionTime, so a 300 s import figure is a sum over files and cannot be read as 300 s of wall clock.

The one structural lever this file offers is sharding rather than trimming: the 58 self-resetting tests can move into separate files each with its own sandbox, estimated at roughly 400 s down to 120-150 s wall on this machine, which must be measured rather than claimed.

direction: Cutting node startup to speed up upgrade-legacy
reason: Measured at 0.020 s per start, so eliminating every spawn saves seconds, not minutes
35.8 MB of 3115 files paid once in beforeAll cannot explain a 400 s file

direction: Removing the second validation pass in upgrade-legacy
reason: It is the proof that a repair worked; removing it drops an assertion the file exists to make

label: The packet's third open item treats the core lane's import time as a cost to cut, while Vitest reports it as a per-file sum; the two readings disagree and the question stays open
